paper.note: The page ground. Dark is a near-black rather than pure black, so the plate has somewhere to lighten to.

ink.note: All text, every heading, the one filled button, the focus outline, the Curated mark, and the ::selection background.

muted.note: Gathered facts, captions, provenance, inactive navigation. Quiet, still legible at 0.75rem.

rule.note: Every 1px separator, the field underline at rest, and link decoration colour before hover.

inverse.note: Text on an ink fill. Equal to paper in both themes, but named separately so a fill never has to name the page's colour.

plate.note: The ground a photograph is mounted on, a hair off paper. On dark it lightens away from the page rather than darkening, so an image still reads as mounted.

danger.note: The only hue in the system. Error text under a form, and nothing else — never a badge, a status, or a decoration.

display.purpose: A Brand's name on its own page. Measured at 80px, weight 300, letter-spacing -1.6px at full width. Steps to weight 400 on dark.

annotation.purpose: The judgement — the largest prose a Curated Brand page carries. Never truncated, clamped, or labelled.

headline.purpose: The h1 of every page that is not a Brand. The homepage runs a wider clamp(2.5rem, 6.5vw, 4.5rem).

title.purpose: Every section h2, always sitting directly under a hairline rule.

price.purpose: The price band on a Brand page — the only place the grotesque is set large, because a number is a gathered fact and must not borrow the serif's authority.

body.purpose: Supporting prose and empty states, capped at 30-36rem (55-69ch).

fact.purpose: The facts line under a Brand name, card titles, card prices, navigation, footer.

micro.purpose: Figure captions, source attribution, option counts, stock state.

fonts.name: Noto Serif Display
fonts.note: Cyrillic is a requirement, not a bonus: a Ukrainian locale is coming and a display face that cannot set a Brand's name in Ukrainian would have to be replaced.

elevation.note: Every computed border-radius in the app is 0px and every computed box-shadow is none, in both themes and on every surface including the one modal overlay. Depth is a hairline rule, a change of ground (plate), or nothing at all. The dialog uses a bg-ink/60 scrim plus a 1px ink border in place of a shadow.

motion.name: transition-default
motion.purpose: The single transition in the system (Tailwind's `transition`). Applied to colour, opacity, and text-decoration-color on hover. Nothing translates, scales, or animates on entry.

focus.purpose: One focus treatment for the whole site, applied to a, button, input, select and textarea via :focus-visible. Visible on both grounds.

containers.name: page
containers.note: max-w-6xl with a 24px gutter — homepage, drops index, Brand page.

containers.name: watch
containers.note: max-w-4xl — one Watch page, whose subject is one photograph and one list.

aspectRatios.name: brand-lead
aspectRatios.note: Figure column, 768x540 including a 12px caption. Deliberately not a full-width banner.

narrative.overview:
This is a reference you consult about brands, not a shop that sells them. The world is paper white, near-black ink, and one hairline rule — the arrangement a serious reference work has used for a century, taken deliberately rather than inherited. It was chosen over five invented alternatives with A Collected Man and Hodinkee named as the craft bar, and the anti-reference is explicit: the dark, gold-lit luxury-watch page where atmosphere stands in for having a view. Nothing here glows. Nothing is dressed up. A page earns attention by saying something true in a large enough size to be read.

The defining constraint is that there is no accent colour at all. Seven tokens carry the entire system and six of them are neutral; the seventh is an error red that never decorates anything. Photographs are the only colour on the page, and they are a brand's own watches, which is the only colour a reference about watches should be spending. That single refusal does most of the work: with no brand hue to reach for, hierarchy has to come from size, weight, ground, and the space around a thing — which is what makes the layout legible rather than styled.

The surface is flat in the literal sense: every computed border-radius in the app is 0px and every computed box-shadow is none, in both themes, on every surface, including the one overlay. An object is separated from the page by a hairline rule, by a change of ground, or by nothing at all. Two faces divide the labour honestly — a light high-contrast serif for the two things a person actually wrote (a Brand's name and the judgement about it), and a neutral grotesque for every fact the machines gathered. A reader can tell opinion from data without being told which is which.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-white ground, near-black ink, one hairline rule (19.68:1 on paper)
No accent colour; photographs supply all colour on the page
Zero radius, zero shadow, everywhere, in both themes
Serif for authored prose, grotesque for gathered fact
Light is the considered palette; dark is re-derived, not inverted
Filled elements are rare and earned; links are underlines
Empty states are plain sentences, never dashed placeholder boxes

rules.name: The Seven Tokens Rule
rules.body: Every colour in the app comes from one of seven --cw-* tokens. No component carries a hex value and no component carries a dark: variant — the theme is resolved once at the root by light-dark(), so a component written correctly is already correct in both worlds.

rules.name: The No Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no accent colour. Photographs are the only colour on the page. If a new surface needs emphasis, it gets size, ink, a rule, or a fill — never a hue.

rules.name: The Considered Light Rule
rules.body: Light is the designed palette; dark is re-derived from it, not inverted. Two values are re-thought rather than flipped: the display weight steps 300 → 400 (--dark-display-weight), because a light serif that is elegant on paper turns to wire on black; and the plate lightens away from the page instead of darkening.

rules.name: The Danger-Is-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: The one non-neutral token is reserved for errors. A status, a badge, a category, or a call to action never reaches for it.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The serif carries only what a person wrote — a Brand's name and the judgement. Everything gathered by a machine is set in the grotesque. A price, a country, a founding year, or a drop title in the serif is a category error.

rules.name: The Unlabelled Annotation Rule
rules.body: The Annotation is rendered exactly as written: never truncated, never line-clamped, never faded at the bottom, never appended to. It carries no heading above it — the sentence is the largest prose on the page and the small line beneath it says who wrote it, which is more than a label would. An Annotation that says the lume is poor has to be able to say the lume is poor.

rules.name: The Cyrillic Rule
rules.body: Both faces carry Cyrillic and no layout may depend on English string lengths. Cyrillic runs roughly a third longer; headings wrap, buttons grow, and nothing is sized to a specific English word.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: There are no uppercase letterspaced kickers, eyebrows, or all-caps labels in this system. A section is announced by a rule and a serif h2, and by nothing else.

rules.name: The Section Rhythm Rule
rules.body: New sections use mt-14 + border-t border-rule + pt-10. Do not invent a second separator style; the hairline above a serif h2 is the only section boundary this world has.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose is capped at 30-36rem (55-69ch). Nothing in this system runs the full 72rem as a paragraph.

rules.name: The Laid Out Twice Rule
rules.body: The navigation is composed twice — a desktop row and a named Menu panel below sm — rather than shrunk to fit. Shaving gaps until a row almost fits is how a header ends up with its last control off-screen.

rules.name: The Flat World Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no drop-shadow, no filter: blur() on a surface, ever. If a new element needs to be told apart from the page, use a rule, a plate, or space.

rules.name: The Three Separators Rule
rules.body: A hairline, a change of ground, or nothing at all. An element that needs a fourth kind of separation is an element in the wrong place.

rules.name: The Earned Fill Rule
rules.body: A filled ink rectangle is used only where the action is that section's own subject: the digest form's submit, a store purchase link, the homepage's one route into the catalogue. The header CTA is a text link, because a black rectangle there would be the loudest object in every first viewport on the site — outranking, on a Brand page, the brand's own name.

rules.name: The Normalised Photograph Rule
rules.body: Every image goes through Plate. contain in grids; cover only on a lead photograph. Every lead carries a figcaption naming whose photograph it is.

rules.name: The Plain Empty State Rule
rules.body: An empty state is a sentence in muted body prose that says what is missing and why. No dashed box, no placeholder graphic, no illustration, no icon.

rules.name: The One Focus Rule
rules.body: One focus treatment for the whole site: a 2px solid ink outline at 2px offset on every link, button, input, select and textarea. It is visible on both grounds and is never removed for a custom ring.

dos: Do read every colour from the seven --cw-* tokens; a component written correctly needs no dark: variant.
Do set a Brand's name and the judgement in the display serif, and every gathered fact in Golos Text.
Do separate sections with mt-14 + border-t border-rule + pt-10, and put the serif h2 immediately under the rule.
Do route every image through Plate, contain by default, and caption a lead with "From {brand}'s own store."
Do write empty states as plain sentences that admit what is missing.
Do state a Listed Brand's absence at the size of every other fact, and lead its page with the photograph instead.
Do compose a responsive layout twice when one arrangement cannot serve both 375px and desktop.
Do let both faces' Cyrillic carry the layout — size nothing to an English word.
donts: Don't introduce an accent colour, a brand hue, or a coloured badge. Photographs are the only colour on this page.
Don't add a border-radius or a box-shadow to anything, including overlays. Use a hairline, a plate, or space.
Don't truncate, line-clamp, fade, or append to an Annotation, and don't put a label above it.
Don't put a filled ink button anywhere the action is not that section's own subject — the header CTA stays a text link.
Don't crop a grid image with cover; cover belongs to the Brand lead alone.
Don't wrap a field in a box. A rule under the input is the whole field.
Don't use uppercase letterspaced kickers, eyebrows, or all-caps labels.
Don't draw an icon where a word will do — the mobile menu says Menu.
Don't style a Listed Brand as an error, a warning, or a missing Curated one.
Don't use --cw-danger for anything but error text.
Don't replace an empty state with a dashed placeholder box or an illustration.
